author: ohtadmin
title: Council mulls buying Pemberton site to build affordable housing
text:
The town is negotiating with the owners of 73 Pemberton Ave. to purchase the 36,000-square-foot lot and subdivide the property to support affordable housing.
Town Administrator Ed Mello briefed the town council Monday at its meeting about the pending $475,000 transaction, of which $245,000 would be subsidized through a federal Community Development Block Grant. The remainder would come from the affordable housing committee’s trust fund.
The three councilors in attendance tabled the item due to the absence of Councilwomen Mary Glackin and Mary Meagher.
“I think this is going to pass with no problem,” Vice President Erik Brine said. “But I also realize it’s a pretty significant investment by the community.”
The deal and subsequent subdivision would give the town possession of a 15,300-square-foot parcel. The house currently on this section would be converted into affordable housing.
The current owners, John Preece and Kathryn Koken, would retain the remaining 20,700 square feet.
The pending deal, however, does have an “anomaly,” Mello said. The sellers, after a purchase-and-sales agreement is signed, want an advance of $118,750 prior to closing. Councilman Eddie Ross was concerned about that condition.
“I would presume we would get it back if the deal falls through during the close?” he asked.
Mello, however, said that language was not finalized. “There always is a risk when you advance money,” he added.
Mello, however, said the sides have been negotiating for nearly two years, and they are eager to sell.
“I’m confident they are going to move forward,” he said.
“I’m not close to the deal,” Ross replied, “so I don’t want to be prescriptive. But if there is a remedy, that would probably be a good idea in the event that it falls apart.”
“I agree,” said Mello.
Tabling the matter, Mello added, will allow Town Solicitor Peter Ruggiero to develop language in the meantime that could include a refund clause. Waiting for the full council before a vote is taken will not impact the deal, he added.
